question: What do we mean by 'body mechanics' in nursing and midwifery?

options.A: The safe and efficient use of the body during movement
options.B: The study of joint inflammation and arthritis
options.C: The surgical repair of damaged skeletal muscles
options.D: The physical assessment of a newborn's reflexes

explanation: You use body mechanics every day! It is simply about moving your own body in a smart, safe way so you protect your back and save energy while working. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h1)

question: When lifting a heavy load, why should you pivot with your feet instead of twisting your spine?

options.A: Twisting automatically reduces the base of support to zero
options.B: Twisting places dangerous rotational stress on the spinal discs
options.C: Pivoting helps engage the abdominal muscles for better breathing
options.D: Pivoting with the feet allows the nurse to move twice as fast

explanation: Twisting while carrying weight puts a lot of pressure on your lower back discs. Turning your whole body with your feet keeps your spine happy and safe! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is the very first thing you should check before moving a patient from a bed to a wheelchair?

options.A: Administer a mild sedative to calm the patient down
options.B: Ask the patient's relatives to perform the entire transfer
options.C: Assess the patient's mobility and ability to cooperate
options.D: Lower the hospital bed to the lowest floor position

explanation: Always check what your patient can do on their own first. It helps you know how much support they need and keeps both of you safe. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h2)

question: You are helping a postpartum mother move up in bed. Which action shows great body mechanics?

options.A: Twisting the torso quickly to gain momentum before lifting
options.B: Lifting with straight knees while arching the back backward
options.C: Bending at the knees and keeping the patient close to the chest
options.D: Keeping feet close together and bending directly at the waist

explanation: Using your strong leg muscles (by bending your knees) and keeping the patient close prevents back strain. Let your legs do the heavy lifting! [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h2)

question: To keep the skin healthy and prevent pressure sores, how often should an immobile patient be repositioned?
explanation: Turning patients every two hours takes the pressure off bony areas, keeping their skin safe and healthy. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h3)

question: What common problem happens if a bedridden patient's feet are left dangling or unsupported for too long?
explanation: Without a support like a footboard, gravity points the toes downward, which can tighten the calf muscles and lead to foot drop. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of a trochanter roll when positioning a patient?

options.A: To prevent the external rotation of the patient's hips
options.B: To support the lower back during heavy lifting
options.C: To prevent the patient from sliding down the bed
options.D: To keep the heels elevated off the mattress surface

explanation: A trochanter roll is placed snugly beside the thighs to stop the legs from rolling outward when a patient is resting in bed. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which simple device is best for preventing foot drop in a patient who cannot move?
explanation: A firm footboard at the end of the bed gives the soles of the feet a flat surface to rest against, keeping them in a normal upright position. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to protect your back as a midwife?

options.A: Maintaining a wide base of support with feet comfortably apart
options.B: Asking a colleague to assist with heavy or uncooperative patients
options.C: Bending directly at the waist to pick up heavy items from the floor
options.D: Using mechanical lift devices whenever available and necessary

explanation: Bending at the waist puts all the strain on your lower back! Always bend your knees instead to protect your spine. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why are slide sheets so helpful when moving a patient across from a bed to a trolley?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for more than one staff member
options.B: They keep the patient warm during the transfer procedure
options.C: They automatically lift the patient into the air without human effort
options.D: They significantly reduce surface friction between the patient and the bed

explanation: Slide sheets make the surface slippery, allowing you to glide the patient smoothly without straining your back or dragging their skin. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T5#BMP110_U4_T5_h5)
